events.title: DEA permanently schedules N-desethyl isotonitazene and N-piperidinyl etonitazene in Schedule I
events.summary: The Drug Enforcement Administration issued a final order permanently placing N-desethyl isotonitazene and N-piperidinyl etonitazene in Schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act, effective January 22, 2026. These synthetic opioids, which have no accepted medical use in the United States, were temporarily scheduled in July 2024 due to imminent public safety hazards. The NDAA authorizes defense spending and military policy for the fiscal year. As the primary annual defense legislation, it sets military budgets, personnel policies, and strategic directives. The bill's passage reflects congressional exercise of its constitutional power of the purse over military affairs.
events.why_relevant: The NDAA is the foundational annual statute governing U.S. military structure, spending, and operations; its enactment affirms congressional control over defense policy and military resource allocation.

events.title: EPA establishes pesticide tolerance for thiamethoxam residues on imported black pepper
events.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency finalized a rule establishing a tolerance of 0.15 parts per million (ppm) for residues of the insecticide thiamethoxam on black pepper, in response to a petition by the American Spice Trade Association. The tolerance exceeds the petitioner's requested 0.1 ppm based on monitoring data. EPA conducted aggregate risk assessments and determined that the tolerance poses no reasonable certainty of harm to the general population or to infants and children from dietary, drinking water, and residential exposures combined.
events.why_relevant: Pesticide tolerance-setting directly affects food safety standards, agricultural commerce, and consumer exposure to chemical residues in imported commodities.

events.title: EPA establishes time-limited pesticide tolerances for flupyradifurone on sugarcane under FIFRA emergency exemption
events.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency issued a final rule establishing time-limited tolerances for residues of flupyradifurone on sugarcane commodities in response to a crisis exemption granted under the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act. The rule sets maximum permissible residue levels at 3 parts per million for sugarcane cane and 90 ppm for sugarcane molasses, effective immediately. The tolerances expire December 31, 2028. EPA determined the pesticide poses no unreasonable risk to the general population or infants and children based on aggregate exposure assessment.
events.why_relevant: EPA's emergency tolerance-setting authority under FIFRA section 18 and FFDCA section 408(l)(6) bypasses normal notice-and-comment rulemaking, concentrating regulatory power in the executive branch without public participation in pesticide safety determinations affecting food supply.
events.basis: This regulation establishes time-limited tolerances for residues of flupyradifurone, including its metabolites and degradates, in or on sugarcane, cane and sugarcane, molasses. This action is in response to EPA's concurrence of a crisis exemption under the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA) authorizing use of the pesticide on sugarcane.

events.title: EPA issues cancellation order for pesticide registrations and use amendments
events.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency issued a final cancellation order under the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA) for 27 pesticide product registrations and amendments to terminate specific uses for 14 additional products, effective December 19, 2025. The cancellations and amendments were voluntarily requested by registrants and followed a 30-day public comment period (August 5 to September 4, 2025) during which EPA received no substantive comments. One registrant withdrew their request and was removed from the order. Existing stocks may be sold under specified timelines: 1 year for Table 1 products, 18 months for Table 1A and Table 2 products.
events.why_relevant: This regulatory action affects pesticide availability and agricultural/commercial practices, with implications for environmental protection, public health, and industry compliance with federal pesticide law.
events.basis: EPA hereby approves the requested cancellations and/or amendments to terminate uses of registrations identified in Tables 1, 1A and 2 of Unit II. events.title: FCC adopts final rule revising Low Power Television, TV Translator, and Class A Television Service regulations
events.summary: The Federal Communications Commission adopted a final rule amending 47 CFR Parts 11, 73, and 74 to modernize regulations governing Low Power Television (LPTV), TV Translator, and Class A television stations. Changes include revised facility relocation distance limits (49.1 km), formalized community-of-license designations, standardized call sign requirements, clarified video program signal definitions, Emergency Alert System obligation clarifications, channel 14 emission mask requirements, prohibition on operations above channel 36, and streamlined displacement procedures.
